Q: Is there a SPRING batch equivalent in .NET A:

For your exact use case (flat file ingestion, transform, export), most .NET teams historically cobbled something together themselves since there's no canonical equivalent to Spring Batch in the ecosystem.

I faced the same dilemma when looking for a Spring Batch equivalent for .NET and couldn't find any, so I built NBatch (https://www.nuget.org/packages/NBatch), which is inspired by Spring Batch. It follows the reader → processor → writer model, handles job state and restartability, and is designed for exactly this kind of flat file pipeline.

For 10 million rows you don't need big data infrastructure, but you do want chunk-based processing so you're not loading everything into memory. Whatever you pick, make sure it supports that.

Q: Row filtering a QTableWidget in PyQt5 A:

I couldn't test it but I think you have to remove if not match: break because it may stop filtering after first iteration.

In old version you have two nested for-loop so break is existing loop for column but not loop for row.

In new version you have only loop for rows so break can be useless - it exists after first non-matching row and it doesn't check others.

Q: Edit Excel Checkbox so that it displays a X rather than a tick when the value is true A:

There is a way to do this, but you're not going to be using a real checkbox. Select the cell where you want the checkbox to display and then in your Insert ribbon select "Symbols". Select Wingdings as your font and search through the symbols for an empty box and a box with an "X", ("o" and "ý"). These are going to be your "not a real checkbox" checkbox states. Create a VBA routine that checks to makes sure that you are in a valid cell and then toggle the character between "o" and "ý" and select a different cell (the one time I had to do this, I just selected the adjacent cell which contained the text for my checkbox) and fire the routine on the SelectionChange event. If your real checkbox is tied to a cell, you just need to add a formula to that cell that checks for which character is present.

Q: How do I prevent testify command line args from leaking into my Cobra application? A:

Your test depends on os.Args[1:] and this the reason you have this problem.

cobra package - github.com/spf13/cobra - Go Packages

func (*Command) Execute ¶

func (c *Command) Execute() error

Execute uses the args (os.Args[1:] by default) and run through the command tree finding appropriate matches for commands and then corresponding flags.

Test should never depend on global state, so you have to correct test. Note tat doc above says this is os.Args[1:] is used by default. So to fix it alternative value has to be provided, so default will not kick in.

In documentation you can find way to overcome this:

cobra package - github.com/spf13/cobra - Go Packages

func (*Command) SetArgs ¶

func (c *Command) SetArgs(a []string)

SetArgs sets arguments for the command. It is set to os.Args[1:] by default, if desired, can be overridden particularly useful when testing.

So it clearly documented to use SetArgs when testing.
